title: Trim the Front in Threes Until Unique
statement:
You get an integer array nums. One operation removes the first three elements, or all remaining elements if fewer than three are left.

Return the minimum number of operations needed until all remaining elements are distinct. An empty array counts as distinct, and if nums is already distinct the answer is 0.

examples.why: Removing [4, 2, 4] leaves [1, 5, 2, 6]. One cut drops the first copy of both 4 and 2.
After one operation [7, 7] is left, still with a repeat. The second operation empties the array.
Already distinct, so nothing is removed.

hints: Operations only ever remove from the front. So the array after k operations is just the suffix starting at index 3k.
Which suffixes are distinct? If a suffix starting at i is distinct, so is every shorter one. Find the longest distinct suffix.
Scan from the right with a set. The first index whose value is already in the set marks where duplicates start: you must cut past it.

explain.intuition:
After k operations the array is exactly nums[3k ..]. So the question is: what is the smallest k whose suffix has no repeats?

Scan from the right end adding values to a set. The first time you meet a value already in the set, at index i, you know that any suffix that still contains index i has a duplicate, while the suffix starting at i + 1 is clean. You need 3k > i, so k = floor(i / 3) + 1. If the scan never finds a repeat, the answer is 0.
steps: If nums[i] is already in the set, return floor(i / 3) + 1.
Otherwise add it and continue. If the loop finishes, return 0.
pitfalls: Returning the number of duplicate values instead of operations. Each operation removes three items, not one repeat.
Scanning from the left and stopping at the first repeat. The last repeated position is what matters, since everything before it must go.
Off by one in the formula: with the repeat at index 3, one operation keeps index 3, so you need floor(3 / 3) + 1 = 2.

solutions.title: Simulate the removals
solutions.idea: While the remaining suffix has a repeat, cut three more from the front and check again.

solutions.title: Scan from the right with a set
solutions.idea: The first repeat met from the right, at index i, must be removed; that takes floor(i / 3) + 1 operations.

followups: Each operation removes the first c elements instead of three. What changes in the formula?
You may remove from either end, three at a time. How would you find the fewest operations then?
lcTitle: Minimum Number of Operations to Make Elements in Array Distinct
